The main takeaway from our work is that

the performance of distributed simulators is fundamentally limited by the instability of message sequencers, and that the performance of optimistic resequencing algorithms is limited by the instability and performance limits of message sequencers.

distributed simulation of feedforward queueings networks with optimistic resequencing and without flow control is unstable, and the throughput of such simulators is limited by the rate at which messages arrive at the sequencers.

, in the absence of interprocessor flow control, the throughput of distributed simulations of open feedforward networks with conservative sequencing, or with optimistic resequencing without flow control, is limited by the maximum lookahead of the sequencing algorithm, rather than the network size.
